scope: Art-only handoff: stand-up, walk, kneeling and standing falls for the accepted partisan rifleman.
referenceRecipe: First cell of the accepted four-column/two-row atlas, rounded crop from fractional 443.5px geometry; original file unchanged.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / game animation extension. The reference is the EXACT accepted partisan rifleman: adult small pale face, brown hair, soft olive PARTISAN FIELD CAP with tiny red star (NO HELMET or beret), light khaki-green tunic with dark collar/straps and belt pouches, dark olive trousers, brown leather high boots, and a LONG BROWN WOODEN-STOCK RIFLE pointing SCREEN RIGHT. Preserve this exact identity, costume, weapon length, chunky dark outlined small-game pixel-art treatment, limited flat olive/khaki/brown palette, small face and adult proportions. This is NOT a realistic painted soldier or a style upgrade. Keep transparent margins truly alpha-zero, without soft glow, shadows, floor stripe, scenery, text, captions, numbers, checkerboard or cell borders. No muzzle flash, smoke, bullets or blood.
Deliver ONLY TWELVE new animation poses in EXACTLY FOUR columns by THREE rows on a 1536x1536 TRANSPARENT canvas (cells 384x512). Within EACH cell use a fixed sprite rectangle x=0..383, y=16..495 (384x480), representing a 128x160 game frame at exactly 3x magnification. A fixed common contact floor is at cell-local y=427; actor root x=192. Match the scale of the reference body rather than independently stretching each pose: kneeling body height about 218 pixels, standing body height about 345 pixels, cap width about 67 pixels. Reference kneeling head top is around cell y=210, standing head top around y=82; boots always meet y=427. Rifle and all limbs must fit inside each own cell with empty margins. Keep character root and camera fixed in every cell.
TOP ROW: four sequential STAND-UP transition frames starting from the reference KNEELING aim stance. 1 exact kneeling ready pose with rifle aimed right. 2 lower rifle from shoulder to safe low carry with both hands, tuck the kneeling leg under body. 3 push up through the planted front boot, torso and hips rise naturally, rear knee lifts from the ground. 4 fully upright standing carry stance, rifle held diagonally across chest at low ready, not aiming or firing. Preserve anatomical limb lengths: standing makes him taller because the knees extend, not because the body is resized.
MIDDLE AND BOTTOM ROWS: EIGHT-frame WALK LOOP IN PLACE of the now-standing SAME soldier carrying SAME rifle at low ready, muzzle safely pointing forward-right slightly down, hands fixed to the rifle. Only normal small body bob (at most 2 game pixels). In order: left-foot forward/right back contact; weight/down; right passing left support; right swinging/up; right-foot forward/left back contact; weight/down; left passing right support; left swinging/up back into first contact. BOTH legs must visibly alternate. Fixed support floor y=427, no horizontal travel, no sliding like a stiff cutout, no running, no kneeling in these eight walk cells. Keep consistent cap/head size, body mass, rifle and position across the whole sheet. Whole sprites stay separated and unclipped. The standing fourth transition frame must blend naturally into the walk loop.

prompts.prompt:

Correct the rifle length: it has become a short carbine in image 1, whereas the original is a clearly long wooden-stock rifle. In EVERY cell increase its visible stock-to-muzzle length by about 40% relative to the soldier's head and torso, while keeping its brown stock, dark barrel, metal bands, and correct grips. Keep the soldier the SAME character, original cap with red star, khaki tunic, olive trousers, brown boots and exact face size relative to body.
To leave room for this longer rifle WITHOUT crossing any cell boundary, first make the WHOLE figure and equipment about 75% of its current source size uniformly in every cell, then extend the rifle relative to that smaller figure. Keep the standing-to-kneeling anatomical height relationship. This reduced source size is intentional; the game will use one fixed enlargement when packing. At the new scale the first kneeling pose must match image 2's relative anatomy and weapon length. Use the same ground contact line at 93% of cell height in all three rows, keep each actor's hip horizontally stationary through its sequence. Do not rescale poses individually. Frame1 is still kneeling aim, frames2–4 still stand up, and frames5–12 still eight progressive walking phases in place, rifle at safe low carry. Retain clearly alternating left/right legs. No running or extra states. Do not change camera, outfit, palette or chunky small-game pixel drawing style. Full figures and rifle tips must stay within their own cells with transparent margins. Truly transparent alpha-zero background only, hard opaque sprite pixels without glow, labels, frame borders or shadows.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / game fall-animation extension. The reference is the EXACT accepted partisan rifleman: adult small pale face, brown hair, soft olive PARTISAN FIELD CAP with tiny red star (NO HELMET or beret), light khaki-green tunic with dark collar/straps and belt pouches, dark olive trousers, brown leather high boots, and a LONG BROWN WOODEN-STOCK RIFLE pointing SCREEN RIGHT. Preserve this exact identity, costume, weapon length, chunky dark outlined small-game pixel-art treatment, limited flat olive/khaki/brown palette, small face and adult proportions. This is NOT a realistic painted soldier or a style upgrade. Keep transparent margins truly alpha-zero, without soft glow, shadows, floor stripe, scenery, text, captions, numbers, checkerboard or cell borders. No muzzle flash, smoke, bullets or blood.
Deliver SIX progressive non-looping DEATH/FALL poses, exactly THREE equal columns by TWO equal rows, on a transparent 1536x1024 canvas (cells 512x512). Within EACH cell the virtual sprite rectangle is x=64..447, y=16..495 (384x480), representing the same 128x160 game frame at 3x. Fixed floor at cell-local y=427; stationary body root near cell x=256. Scale remains fixed throughout: the reference KNEELING pose is about 218 pixels high and its cap about 67 pixels wide. No scaling the last fallen figure to fill space.
This is a fall FROM THE EXISTING KNEELING FIRING STANCE, not a standing soldier. Keep the long rifle in the hands until he loses support, then let it settle visibly beside him; do not vanish it. 1 small startled impact reaction while still kneeling, lower shoulder and rifle just a little. 2 torso curls forward and sideways toward screen right, front leg buckles, rifle muzzle drops. 3 free hand reaches the ground to brace as hips move off the rear heel, long rifle held safely diagonally so it fits. 4 hips and side meet the floor, torso tipping onto the right side, knees bent in front rather than rigidly spinning the whole sprite. 5 head/shoulder settle close to the floor with knees curled, rifle beside his body, no bounce. 6 final completely motionless SIDE-LYING body, cap stays on, bent legs and attached clothing unchanged, same recognizable long rifle lying alongside. Body and rifle stay entirely inside the virtual 384x480 sprite rectangle (x64..447), not crossing cell borders. During the fall feet, supporting hand and then hip/side contact the SAME floor, no hovering; no vertical movement of the floor. Final frame must hold indefinitely. No gore, no blood, no explosion or hit stars. Give a clearly readable progression, not six identical sleeping figures.
prompts.selection: Selected progressive kneeling fall; last side-lying pose holds.

prompts.prompt:
Create SIX progressive non-looping FALL/DEATH frames for the EXACT partisan rifleman from image 1, STARTING FROM STANDING LOW CARRY. Image1 is the authoritative prepared standing pose; image2 is the original accepted character's clothing/rifle identity. Same adult small pale face, brown hair, soft PARTISAN CAP with tiny red star, light khaki-green tunic with brown belt and pouches, dark olive trousers, brown high boots, LONG brown wooden-stock rifle. Same crisp small-game dark-outline pixel art, no detailed realistic rendering, helmet or new gear. Keep cap ON and keep the same rifle visible through the fall. No blood, gore, impact stars, muzzle flash, smoke, scenery, text, grid or shadows. Truly transparent alpha-zero background with hard opaque sprite pixels, no soft halo.
Layout EXACTLY 3 columns by 2 rows on 1536x1024. Each cell is 512x512. Within each cell the virtual sprite rectangle is x=64..447, y=16..495, corresponding to a 128x160 game frame at 3x scale. Root at cell x=256, visible floor at y=427. Standing body is about 285px high and the same size in all frames; do NOT resize later fallen poses. Boots, then knee/hand, then side contact this fixed floor. Keep whole body, cap and long rifle inside x=64..447 and y=16..495, no cell crossing. Let the body naturally settle to the RIGHT side; keep knees bent so the final body fits.
Frame1: nearly the exact standing low-carry pose from image1, a small recoil/startle, both boots planted, rifle across front with muzzle low-right. Frame2: knees buckle, hips lower and torso curls forward-right; one boot slides slightly but body root does not travel away. Frame3: one knee drops to floor, free support hand reaches down, rifle stays beside torso. Frame4: hips and right side reach ground, shoulders tipping down, knees bent. Frame5: body settles almost on side, head close to ground, long rifle lies diagonally alongside. Frame6: clearly final motionless side-lying fallen pose with bent knees, cap retained, rifle alongside. The body must bend and change silhouette anatomically; no rigid rotation of standing cutout. Read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. All six figures are exactly the same anatomical scale and camera angle. Frame6 must hold indefinitely.
